title: अंश ४ · अध्याय ४

items.text: (सगरस्य अश्वमेधयज्ञः, सौदासचरित्रम्, रामचरित्रम्)
items.tr: (sagarasya aśvamedhayajñaḥ, saudāsacaritram, rāmacaritram)

items.speaker: श्रीपराशर उवाच
items.text: काश्यपदुहिता सुमतिः विदर्भराजतनया केशिनी च द्वे भार्ये सगरस्य आस्ताम् ॥१॥
items.tr: kāśyapaduhitā sumatiḥ vidarbharājatanayā keśinī ca dve bhārye sagarasya āstām ||1||

items.text: ताभ्यां चापत्यार्थम् और्वः परमेण समाधिनाराधितो वरम् अदात् ॥२॥
items.tr: tābhyāṃ cāpatyārtham aurvaḥ parameṇa samādhinārādhito varam adāt ||2||

items.text: “एका वंशकरमेकं पुत्रम्, अपरा षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणां जनयिष्यतीति यस्या यदभिमतं तदिच्छया गृह्यताम्” इत्युक्ते केशिनी एकं वरयामास ॥३॥
items.tr: “ekā vaṃśakaramekaṃ putram, aparā ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇāṃ janayiṣyatīti yasyā yadabhimataṃ tadicchayā gṛhyatām” ityukte keśinī ekaṃ varayāmāsa ||3||

items.text: सुमतिः पुत्रसहस्राणि षष्टिं वव्रे ॥४॥
items.tr: sumatiḥ putrasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭiṃ vavre ||4||

items.text: “तथा” इत्युक्ते अल्पैरहोभिः केशिनी पुत्रम् एकम् असमञ्जसनामानं वंशकरम् असूत ॥५॥
items.tr: “tathā” ityukte alpairahobhiḥ keśinī putram ekam asamañjasanāmānaṃ vaṃśakaram asūta ||5||

items.text: काश्यपतनयायाः तु सुमत्याः षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्रणि अभवन् ॥६॥
items.tr: kāśyapatanayāyāḥ tu sumatyāḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasraṇi abhavan ||6||

items.text: तस्मात् असमञ्जसात् अंशुमान् नाम कुमारो जज्ञे ॥७॥
items.tr: tasmāt asamañjasāt aṃśumān nāma kumāro jajñe ||7||

items.text: स त्वसमञ्जसो बालो बाल्यादेव असद्वृत्तोऽभूत् ॥८॥
items.tr: sa tvasamañjaso bālo bālyādeva asadvṛtto'bhūt ||8||

items.text: पिता चास्य अचिन्तयत् “अयम् अतीतबाल्यः सुबुद्धिमान् भविष्यति” इति ॥९॥
items.tr: pitā cāsya acintayat “ayam atītabālyaḥ subuddhimān bhaviṣyati” iti ||9||

items.text: अथ तत्रापि च वयसि अतीते असच्चरितमेनं पिता तत्याज ॥१०॥
items.tr: atha tatrāpi ca vayasi atīte asaccaritamenaṃ pitā tatyāja ||10||

items.text: तान्यपि षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि असमञ्जसचरितमेव अनुचक्रुः ॥११॥
items.tr: tānyapi ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi asamañjasacaritameva anucakruḥ ||11||

items.text: ततश्च असमञ्जसचरितानुकारिभिः सागरैः अपध्वस्तयज्ञादिसन्मार्गे जगति देवाः सकलविद्यामयम् असंस्पृष्टम् अशेषदोषैः भगवतः पुरुषोत्तमस्य अंशभूतं कपिलं प्रणम्य तदर्थम् ऊचुः ॥१२॥
items.tr: tataśca asamañjasacaritānukāribhiḥ sāgaraiḥ apadhvastayajñādisanmārge jagati devāḥ sakalavidyāmayam asaṃspṛṣṭam aśeṣadoṣaiḥ bhagavataḥ puruṣottamasya aṃśabhūtaṃ kapilaṃ praṇamya tadartham ūcuḥ ||12||

items.text: “भगवन् एभिः सगरतनयैः असमञ्जसचरितम् अनुगम्यते ॥१३॥
items.tr: “bhagavan ebhiḥ sagaratanayaiḥ asamañjasacaritam anugamyate ||13||

items.text: कथमेभिः असद्वृत्तम् अनुसरद्भिः जगद्भविष्यतीति ॥१४॥
items.tr: kathamebhiḥ asadvṛttam anusaradbhiḥ jagadbhaviṣyatīti ||14||

items.text: अत्यार्तजगत्परित्राणाय च भगवतोऽत्र शरीरग्रहणम्” इत्याकर्ण्य भगवानाह “अल्पैरैव दिनैर्विनङ्क्ष्यन्ति” इति ॥१५॥
items.tr: atyārtajagatparitrāṇāya ca bhagavato'tra śarīragrahaṇam” ityākarṇya bhagavānāha “alpairaiva dinairvinaṅkṣyanti” iti ||15||

items.text: अत्रान्तरे च सगरो हयमेधम् आरभत ॥१६॥
items.tr: atrāntare ca sagaro hayamedham ārabhata ||16||

items.text: तस्य च पुत्रैः अधिष्ठितम् अस्य अश्वं कोऽप्यपहृत्य भुवो बिलं प्रविवेश ॥१७॥
items.tr: tasya ca putraiḥ adhiṣṭhitam asya aśvaṃ ko'pyapahṛtya bhuvo bilaṃ praviveśa ||17||

items.text: ततः तत्तनयाश्च अश्वखुरगतिनिर्बन्धेन अवनीम् एकैको योजनं चख्नुः ॥१८॥
items.tr: tataḥ tattanayāśca aśvakhuragatinirbandhena avanīm ekaiko yojanaṃ cakhnuḥ ||18||

items.text: पाताले चाश्वं परिभ्रमन्तं तम् अवनीपतितनयास्ते ददृशुः ॥१९॥
items.tr: pātāle cāśvaṃ paribhramantaṃ tam avanīpatitanayāste dadṛśuḥ ||19||

items.text: नातिदूरेऽवस्थितं च भगवन्तम् अपघने शरत्कालेऽर्कमिव तेजोभिः अवनतमूर्धम् अधश्च अशेषदिशश्च उद्भासयमानं हयहर्त्तारं कपिलर्षिम् अपश्यन् ॥२०॥
items.tr: nātidūre'vasthitaṃ ca bhagavantam apaghane śaratkāle'rkamiva tejobhiḥ avanatamūrdham adhaśca aśeṣadiśaśca udbhāsayamānaṃ hayaharttāraṃ kapilarṣim apaśyan ||20||

items.text: ततश्च उद्यतायुधा “दुरात्मायम् अस्मदपकारी यज्ञविघ्नकारी हन्यतां हयहर्त्ता हन्यताम्” इति अवोचन् अभ्यधावंश्च ॥२१॥
items.tr: tataśca udyatāyudhā “durātmāyam asmadapakārī yajñavighnakārī hanyatāṃ hayaharttā hanyatām” iti avocan abhyadhāvaṃśca ||21||

items.text: ततस्तेनापि भगवता किञ्चित् ईषत्परिवर्त्तितलोचनेन अवलोकिताः स्वशरीरसमुत्थेन अग्निना दह्यमाना विनेशुः ॥२२॥
items.tr: tatastenāpi bhagavatā kiñcit īṣatparivarttitalocanena avalokitāḥ svaśarīrasamutthena agninā dahyamānā vineśuḥ ||22||

items.text: सगरोऽपि अवगम्य अश्वानुसारि तत्पुत्रबलम् अशेषं परमर्षिणा कपिलेन तेजसा दग्धं ततो अंशुमन्तम् असमञ्जसपुत्रम् अश्वानयनाय युयोज ॥२३॥
items.tr: sagaro'pi avagamya aśvānusāri tatputrabalam aśeṣaṃ paramarṣiṇā kapilena tejasā dagdhaṃ tato aṃśumantam asamañjasaputram aśvānayanāya yuyoja ||23||

items.text: स तु सगरतनयखातमार्गेण कपिलमुपगम्य भक्तिनम्रस्तदा तृष्टाव ॥२४॥
items.tr: sa tu sagaratanayakhātamārgeṇa kapilamupagamya bhaktinamrastadā tṛṣṭāva ||24||

items.text: अथैनं भगवानाह ॥२५॥
items.tr: athainaṃ bhagavānāha ||25||

items.text: “गच्छैनं पितामहाय अश्वं प्रापय, वरं वृणीष्व च, पुत्रक, पौत्राश्च ते स्वर्गाद्गङ्गां भुवम् आनेष्यन्त” इति ॥२६॥
items.tr: “gacchainaṃ pitāmahāya aśvaṃ prāpaya, varaṃ vṛṇīṣva ca, putraka, pautrāśca te svargādgaṅgāṃ bhuvam āneṣyanta” iti ||26||

items.text: अथांशुमानपि “स्वर्यातानां ब्रह्मदण्डहतानाम् अस्मत्पितॄणाम् अस्वर्गयोग्यानां स्वर्गप्राप्तिकरं वरम् अस्माकं प्रयच्छ” इति प्रत्याह ॥२७॥
items.tr: athāṃśumānapi “svaryātānāṃ brahmadaṇḍahatānām asmatpitṝṇām asvargayogyānāṃ svargaprāptikaraṃ varam asmākaṃ prayaccha” iti pratyāha ||27||

items.text: तदाकर्ण्य तं च भगवानाह “उक्तमेवैतत् मयाद्य पौत्रस्ते त्रिदिवाद्गङ्गां भुवम् आनेयिष्यति” इति ॥२८॥
items.tr: tadākarṇya taṃ ca bhagavānāha “uktamevaitat mayādya pautraste tridivādgaṅgāṃ bhuvam āneyiṣyati” iti ||28||

items.text: तदम्भसा च संस्पृष्टेषु अस्थिभस्मसु एते च स्वर्गमारोक्ष्यन्ति ॥२९॥
items.tr: tadambhasā ca saṃspṛṣṭeṣu asthibhasmasu ete ca svargamārokṣyanti ||29||

items.text: भगवद्विष्णुपादाङ्गुष्ठनिर्गतस्य हि जलस्य एतन्माहात्म्यम् ॥३०॥
items.tr: bhagavadviṣṇupādāṅguṣṭhanirgatasya hi jalasya etanmāhātmyam ||30||

items.text: यन्न केवलमभिसन्धिपूर्वकं स्नानाद्युपभोगेषु उपकारकम् अनभिसंहितमपि अपेतप्राणस्य अस्थिचर्मस्नायुकेशाद्युपस्पृष्टं शरीरजमपि पतितं सद्यः शरीरिणं स्वर्गं नयति” इत्युक्तः प्रणम्य भवगते, अश्वमादाय पितामहयज्ञम् आजगाम ॥३१॥
items.tr: yanna kevalamabhisandhipūrvakaṃ snānādyupabhogeṣu upakārakam anabhisaṃhitamapi apetaprāṇasya asthicarmasnāyukeśādyupaspṛṣṭaṃ śarīrajamapi patitaṃ sadyaḥ śarīriṇaṃ svargaṃ nayati” ityuktaḥ praṇamya bhavagate, aśvamādāya pitāmahayajñam ājagāma ||31||

items.text: सगरोऽपि अश्वमासाद्य तं यज्ञं समापयामास ॥३२॥
items.tr: sagaro'pi aśvamāsādya taṃ yajñaṃ samāpayāmāsa ||32||

items.text: सागरं च आत्मजप्रीत्या पुत्रत्वे कल्पितवान् ॥३३॥
items.tr: sāgaraṃ ca ātmajaprītyā putratve kalpitavān ||33||

items.text: तस्यांशुमतो दिलीपः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥३४॥
items.tr: tasyāṃśumato dilīpaḥ putro'bhavat ||34||

items.text: दिलीपस्य भगीरथः योऽसौ गङ्गां स्वर्गादिह आनीय भागीरथीसंज्ञां चकार ॥३५॥
items.tr: dilīpasya bhagīrathaḥ yo'sau gaṅgāṃ svargādiha ānīya bhāgīrathīsaṃjñāṃ cakāra ||35||

items.text: भगीरथात् सुहोत्रः सुहोत्रात् श्रुतः, तस्यापि नाभागः ततोऽम्बरीषः, तत्पुत्रः सिन्धुद्वीपः सिन्धुद्वीपात् अयुतायुः ॥३६॥
items.tr: bhagīrathāt suhotraḥ suhotrāt śrutaḥ, tasyāpi nābhāgaḥ tato'mbarīṣaḥ, tatputraḥ sindhudvīpaḥ sindhudvīpāt ayutāyuḥ ||36||

items.text: तत्पुत्रश्च ऋतुपर्णः, योऽसौ नलसहायो अक्षहृदयज्ञोऽभूत् ॥३७॥
items.tr: tatputraśca ṛtuparṇaḥ, yo'sau nalasahāyo akṣahṛdayajño'bhūt ||37||

items.text: ऋतुपर्णपुत्रः सर्वकामः ॥३८॥
items.tr: ṛtuparṇaputraḥ sarvakāmaḥ ||38||

items.text: तत्तनयः सुदासः ॥३९॥
items.tr: tattanayaḥ sudāsaḥ ||39||

items.text: सुदासात् सौदासो मित्रसहनामा ॥४०॥
items.tr: sudāsāt saudāso mitrasahanāmā ||40||

items.text: स च अटव्यां मृगयार्थी पर्यटन् व्याघ्रद्वयम् अपश्यत् ॥४१॥
items.tr: sa ca aṭavyāṃ mṛgayārthī paryaṭan vyāghradvayam apaśyat ||41||

items.text: ताभ्यां तद्वनम् अपमृगं कृतं मत्वा एकं तयोः बाणेन जघान ॥४२॥
items.tr: tābhyāṃ tadvanam apamṛgaṃ kṛtaṃ matvā ekaṃ tayoḥ bāṇena jaghāna ||42||

items.text: म्रियमाणः च असौ अतिभीषणाकृतिः अतिकरालवदनो राक्षसोऽभूत् ॥४३॥
items.tr: mriyamāṇaḥ ca asau atibhīṣaṇākṛtiḥ atikarālavadano rākṣaso'bhūt ||43||

items.text: द्वितीयोऽपि “प्रतिक्रियां ते करिष्यामि” इत्युक्त्वा अन्तर्धानं जगाम ॥४४॥
items.tr: dvitīyo'pi “pratikriyāṃ te kariṣyāmi” ityuktvā antardhānaṃ jagāma ||44||

items.text: कालेन गच्छता सौदासो यज्ञमयजत् ॥४५॥
items.tr: kālena gacchatā saudāso yajñamayajat ||45||

items.text: परिनिष्ठितयज्ञे आचार्ये वसिष्ठे निष्क्रान्ते तद्रक्षो वसिष्ठरूपम् आस्थाय “यज्ञावसाने मम नरमांसभोजनं देयमिति तत्संस्क्रियतां क्षणात् आगमिष्यामि” इत्युक्त्वा निष्क्रान्तः ॥४६॥
items.tr: pariniṣṭhitayajñe ācārye vasiṣṭhe niṣkrānte tadrakṣo vasiṣṭharūpam āsthāya “yajñāvasāne mama naramāṃsabhojanaṃ deyamiti tatsaṃskriyatāṃ kṣaṇāt āgamiṣyāmi” ityuktvā niṣkrāntaḥ ||46||

items.text: भूयश्च सूदवेषं कृत्वा राजाज्ञया मानुषं मांसं संस्कृत्य राज्ञे न्यवेदयत् ॥४७॥
items.tr: bhūyaśca sūdaveṣaṃ kṛtvā rājājñayā mānuṣaṃ māṃsaṃ saṃskṛtya rājñe nyavedayat ||47||

items.text: असावपि हिरण्यपात्रे मांसमादाय वसिष्ठागमनप्रतीक्षकोऽभवत् ॥४८॥
items.tr: asāvapi hiraṇyapātre māṃsamādāya vasiṣṭhāgamanapratīkṣako'bhavat ||48||

items.text: आगताय वसिष्ठाय निवेदितवान् ॥४९॥
items.tr: āgatāya vasiṣṭhāya niveditavān ||49||

items.text: स चाप्यचिन्तयत् “अहो अस्य राज्ञो दौश्शील्यं येन एतन्मांसम् अस्माकं प्रयच्छति किमेतद्द्रव्यजातम्” इति ध्यानपरोऽभवत् ॥५०॥
items.tr: sa cāpyacintayat “aho asya rājño dauśśīlyaṃ yena etanmāṃsam asmākaṃ prayacchati kimetaddravyajātam” iti dhyānaparo'bhavat ||50||

items.text: अपश्यच्च तन्मांसं मानुषम् ॥५१॥
items.tr: apaśyacca tanmāṃsaṃ mānuṣam ||51||

items.text: अतः क्रोधकलुषीकृतचेता राजनि शापमुत्ससर्ज ॥५२॥
items.tr: ataḥ krodhakaluṣīkṛtacetā rājani śāpamutsasarja ||52||

items.text: “यस्मात् अभोज्यमेतत् अस्मद्विधानां तपस्विनाम् अवगच्छन्नपि भवान् मह्यं ददाति तस्मात् तवैवात्र लोलुपता भविष्यति” इति ॥५३॥
items.tr: “yasmāt abhojyametat asmadvidhānāṃ tapasvinām avagacchannapi bhavān mahyaṃ dadāti tasmāt tavaivātra lolupatā bhaviṣyati” iti ||53||

items.text: अनन्तरं च तेनापि “भगवता एवाभिहितो अस्मि” इत्युक्ते “किं किं मयाभिहितम्” इति मुनिः पुनरपि समाधौ तस्थौ ॥५४॥
items.tr: anantaraṃ ca tenāpi “bhagavatā evābhihito asmi” ityukte “kiṃ kiṃ mayābhihitam” iti muniḥ punarapi samādhau tasthau ||54||

items.text: समाधिविज्ञानावगतार्थः च अनुग्रहं तस्मै चकार “नात्यन्तिकम् एतत् द्वादशाब्दं तव भोजनं भविष्यति” इति ॥५५॥
items.tr: samādhivijñānāvagatārthaḥ ca anugrahaṃ tasmai cakāra “nātyantikam etat dvādaśābdaṃ tava bhojanaṃ bhaviṣyati” iti ||55||

items.text: असावपि प्रतिगृह्योदकाञ्जलिं मुनिशापप्रदानाय उद्यतो “भगवन् अयम् अस्मद्गुरुः नार्हसि एनं कुलदेवताभूतम् आचार्यं शप्तुम्” इति मदयन्त्या स्वपत्न्या प्रसादितः । शस्याम्बुदरक्षणार्थं तच्छापाम्बु नोर्व्यां न चाकाशे चिक्षेप, किं तु तेनैव स्वपादौ सिषेच ॥५६॥
items.tr: asāvapi pratigṛhyodakāñjaliṃ muniśāpapradānāya udyato “bhagavan ayam asmadguruḥ nārhasi enaṃ kuladevatābhūtam ācāryaṃ śaptum” iti madayantyā svapatnyā prasāditaḥ | śasyāmbudarakṣaṇārthaṃ tacchāpāmbu norvyāṃ na cākāśe cikṣepa, kiṃ tu tenaiva svapādau siṣeca ||56||

items.text: तेन च क्रोधाश्रितेनाम्बुना दग्धच्छायौ तत्पादौ कल्माषताम् उपगतौ ततः स कल्माषपादसंज्ञाम् अवाप ॥५७॥
items.tr: tena ca krodhāśritenāmbunā dagdhacchāyau tatpādau kalmāṣatām upagatau tataḥ sa kalmāṣapādasaṃjñām avāpa ||57||

items.text: वसिष्ठशापाच्च षष्ठे षष्ठे काले राक्षसस्वभावमेत्याटव्यां पर्यटन् अनेकशो मानुषान् अभक्षयत् ॥५८॥
items.tr: vasiṣṭhaśāpācca ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe kāle rākṣasasvabhāvametyāṭavyāṃ paryaṭan anekaśo mānuṣān abhakṣayat ||58||

items.text: एकदा तु कञ्चिन्मुनिम् ऋतुकाले भार्यासङ्गतं ददर्श ॥५९॥
items.tr: ekadā tu kañcinmunim ṛtukāle bhāryāsaṅgataṃ dadarśa ||59||

items.text: तयोश्च तमतिभीषणं राक्षसस्वरूपम् अवलोक्य त्रासात् दम्पत्योः प्रधावितयोः ब्राह्मणं जग्राह ॥६०॥
items.tr: tayośca tamatibhīṣaṇaṃ rākṣasasvarūpam avalokya trāsāt dampatyoḥ pradhāvitayoḥ brāhmaṇaṃ jagrāha ||60||

items.text: ततस्सा ब्राह्मणी बहुशः तम् अभियाचितवती ॥६१॥
items.tr: tatassā brāhmaṇī bahuśaḥ tam abhiyācitavatī ||61||

items.text: “प्रसीद इक्ष्वाकुकुलतिलकभूतः त्वं महाराजो मित्रसहो न राक्षसः ॥६२॥
items.tr: “prasīda ikṣvākukulatilakabhūtaḥ tvaṃ mahārājo mitrasaho na rākṣasaḥ ||62||

items.text: नार्हसि स्त्रीधर्मसुखाभिज्ञो मयि अकृतार्थायाम् अस्मद्भर्त्तारं हन्तुम्” इत्येवं बहुप्रकारं तस्यां विलपन्त्यां, व्याघ्रः पशुमिवारण्येऽभिमतं तं ब्राह्मणम् अभक्षयत् ॥६३॥
items.tr: nārhasi strīdharmasukhābhijño mayi akṛtārthāyām asmadbharttāraṃ hantum” ityevaṃ bahuprakāraṃ tasyāṃ vilapantyāṃ, vyāghraḥ paśumivāraṇye'bhimataṃ taṃ brāhmaṇam abhakṣayat ||63||

items.text: ततश्चातिकोपसमन्विता ब्राह्मणी तं राजानं शशाप ॥६४॥
items.tr: tataścātikopasamanvitā brāhmaṇī taṃ rājānaṃ śaśāpa ||64||

items.text: “यस्मादेवं मयि अतृप्तायां त्वया अयं मत्पतिः भक्षितः तस्मात् त्वमपि कामोपभोगप्रवृत्तोऽन्तं प्राप्स्यसि” इति ॥६५॥ शप्त्वा चैवं सा अग्निं प्रविवेश ॥६६॥
items.tr: “yasmādevaṃ mayi atṛptāyāṃ tvayā ayaṃ matpatiḥ bhakṣitaḥ tasmāt tvamapi kāmopabhogapravṛtto'ntaṃ prāpsyasi” iti ||65|| śaptvā caivaṃ sā agniṃ praviveśa ||66||

items.text: ततस्तस्य द्वादशाब्दपर्यये विमुक्तशापस्य स्त्रीविषयाभिलाषिणो मदयन्ती तं स्मारयामास ॥६७॥
items.tr: tatastasya dvādaśābdaparyaye vimuktaśāpasya strīviṣayābhilāṣiṇo madayantī taṃ smārayāmāsa ||67||

items.text: ततः परम् असौ स्त्रीभोगं तत्याज ॥६८॥
items.tr: tataḥ param asau strībhogaṃ tatyāja ||68||

items.text: वसिष्ठश्च अपुत्रेण राज्ञा पुत्रार्थम् अभ्यर्थितो मदयन्त्यां गर्भाधानं चकार ॥६९॥
items.tr: vasiṣṭhaśca aputreṇa rājñā putrārtham abhyarthito madayantyāṃ garbhādhānaṃ cakāra ||69||

items.text: यदा च सप्तवर्षाण्यसौ गर्भो न जज्ञे, ततस्तं गर्भमश्मना सा देवी जघान ॥७०॥
items.tr: yadā ca saptavarṣāṇyasau garbho na jajñe, tatastaṃ garbhamaśmanā sā devī jaghāna ||70||

items.text: पुत्रः च अजायत ॥७१॥
items.tr: putraḥ ca ajāyata ||71||

items.text: तस्य च अश्मक इत्येव नामाभवत् ॥७२॥
items.tr: tasya ca aśmaka ityeva nāmābhavat ||72||

items.text: अश्मकस्य मूलको नाम पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥७३॥
items.tr: aśmakasya mūlako nāma putro'bhavat ||73||

items.text: योऽसौ निःक्षत्रे क्ष्मातलेऽस्मिन् क्रियमाणे स्त्रीभिः विवस्त्राभिः परिवार्य रक्षितः ततः तं नारीकवचम् उदाहरन्ति ॥७४॥
items.tr: yo'sau niḥkṣatre kṣmātale'smin kriyamāṇe strībhiḥ vivastrābhiḥ parivārya rakṣitaḥ tataḥ taṃ nārīkavacam udāharanti ||74||

items.text: मूलकात् दशरथः तस्माच् इलिविलः ततश्च विश्वसहः ॥७५॥
items.tr: mūlakāt daśarathaḥ tasmāc ilivilaḥ tataśca viśvasahaḥ ||75||

items.text: तस्माच्च खट्वाङ्गो योऽसौ देवासुरसङ्ग्रामे देवैः अभ्यर्थितः असुरान् जघान ॥७६॥
items.tr: tasmācca khaṭvāṅgo yo'sau devāsurasaṅgrāme devaiḥ abhyarthitaḥ asurān jaghāna ||76||

items.text: स्वर्गे च कृतप्रियैः देवैः वरग्रहणाय चोदितः प्राह ॥७७॥
items.tr: svarge ca kṛtapriyaiḥ devaiḥ varagrahaṇāya coditaḥ prāha ||77||

items.text: “यद्यवश्यं वरो ग्राह्यः तन्मम आयुः कथ्यताम्” इति ॥७८॥
items.tr: “yadyavaśyaṃ varo grāhyaḥ tanmama āyuḥ kathyatām” iti ||78||

items.text: अनन्तरं च तैरुक्तम् “एकमुहूर्तप्रमाणं तवायुः” इत्युक्तः अथ अस्खलितगतिना विमानेन लघिमादिगुणो मर्त्यलोकम् आगम्य इदमाह ॥७९॥
items.tr: anantaraṃ ca tairuktam “ekamuhūrtapramāṇaṃ tavāyuḥ” ityuktaḥ atha askhalitagatinā vimānena laghimādiguṇo martyalokam āgamya idamāha ||79||

items.text: “यथा न ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सकाशात् आत्मापि मे प्रियतरः, न च स्वधर्मोल्लङ्घनं मया कदाचिदपि अनुष्ठितं, न च सकलदेवमानुषपशुपक्षिवृक्षादिकेषु अच्युतव्यतिरेकवती दृष्टिः मम अभूत्, तथा तमेवं मुनिजनानुस्मृतं भगवन्तम् अस्खलितगतिः प्रापयेयम्” इति अशेषदेवगुरौ भगवति अनिर्द्देश्यवपुषि सत्तामात्रात्मनि आत्मानं परमात्मनि वासुदेवाख्ये युयोज । तत्रैव च लयमवाप ॥८०॥
items.tr: “yathā na brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sakāśāt ātmāpi me priyataraḥ, na ca svadharmollaṅghanaṃ mayā kadācidapi anuṣṭhitaṃ, na ca sakaladevamānuṣapaśupakṣivṛkṣādikeṣu acyutavyatirekavatī dṛṣṭiḥ mama abhūt, tathā tamevaṃ munijanānusmṛtaṃ bhagavantam askhalitagatiḥ prāpayeyam” iti aśeṣadevagurau bhagavati anirddeśyavapuṣi sattāmātrātmani ātmānaṃ paramātmani vāsudevākhye yuyoja | tatraiva ca layamavāpa ||80||

items.text:
अत्रापि श्रूयते श्लोको गीतः सप्तर्षिभिः पुरा ।
खट्वाङ्गेन समो नान्यः कश्चिदुर्व्यां भविष्यति ॥८१॥
items.tr:
atrāpi śrūyate śloko gītaḥ saptarṣibhiḥ purā |
khaṭvāṅgena samo nānyaḥ kaścidurvyāṃ bhaviṣyati ||81||

items.text:
येन स्वर्गादिहागम्य मुहूर्त्तं प्राप्य जीवितम् ।
त्रयोऽभिसंहिता लोका बुद्ध्या सत्येन चैव हि ॥८२॥
items.tr:
yena svargādihāgamya muhūrttaṃ prāpya jīvitam |
trayo'bhisaṃhitā lokā buddhyā satyena caiva hi ||82||

items.text: खट्वाङ्गात् दीर्घबाहुः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥८३॥
items.tr: khaṭvāṅgāt dīrghabāhuḥ putro'bhavat ||83||

items.text: ततो रघुरभवत् ॥८४॥
items.tr: tato raghurabhavat ||84||

items.text: तस्मादपि अजः ॥८५॥
items.tr: tasmādapi ajaḥ ||85||

items.text: अजात् दशरथः ॥८६॥
items.tr: ajāt daśarathaḥ ||86||

items.text: तस्यापि भगवानब्जनाभो जगतः स्थित्यर्थम् आत्मांशेन रामलक्ष्मणभरतशत्रुघ्नरूपेण चतुर्द्धा पुत्रत्वम् आयासीत् ॥८७॥
items.tr: tasyāpi bhagavānabjanābho jagataḥ sthityartham ātmāṃśena rāmalakṣmaṇabharataśatrughnarūpeṇa caturddhā putratvam āyāsīt ||87||

items.text: रामोपि बाल एव विश्वामित्रयागरक्षणाय गच्छन् ताटकां जघान ॥८८॥
items.tr: rāmopi bāla eva viśvāmitrayāgarakṣaṇāya gacchan tāṭakāṃ jaghāna ||88||

items.text: यज्ञे च मारीचम् इषुवाताहतं समुद्रे चिक्षेप ॥८९॥
items.tr: yajñe ca mārīcam iṣuvātāhataṃ samudre cikṣepa ||89||

items.text: सुबाहुप्रमुखांश्च क्षयमनयत् ॥९०॥
items.tr: subāhupramukhāṃśca kṣayamanayat ||90||

items.text: दर्शनमात्रेण अहल्यामपापां चकार ॥९१॥
items.tr: darśanamātreṇa ahalyāmapāpāṃ cakāra ||91||

items.text: जनकगृहे च माहेश्वरं चापम् अनायासेन बभञ्ज ॥९२॥
items.tr: janakagṛhe ca māheśvaraṃ cāpam anāyāsena babhañja ||92||

items.text: सीतामयोनिजां जनकराजतनयां वीर्यशुल्कां लेभे ॥९३॥
items.tr: sītāmayonijāṃ janakarājatanayāṃ vīryaśulkāṃ lebhe ||93||

items.text: सकलक्षत्रियक्षयकारिणम् अशेषहैहयकुलधूमकेतुभूतं च परशुरामम् अपास्तवीर्यबलावलेपं चकार ॥९४॥
items.tr: sakalakṣatriyakṣayakāriṇam aśeṣahaihayakuladhūmaketubhūtaṃ ca paraśurāmam apāstavīryabalāvalepaṃ cakāra ||94||

items.text: पितृवचनाच्च अगणितराज्याभिलाषो भ्रातृभार्यासमेतो वनं प्रविवेश ॥९५॥
items.tr: pitṛvacanācca agaṇitarājyābhilāṣo bhrātṛbhāryāsameto vanaṃ praviveśa ||95||

items.text: विराधखरदूषणादीन् कबन्धवालिनौ च निजघान ॥९६॥
items.tr: virādhakharadūṣaṇādīn kabandhavālinau ca nijaghāna ||96||

items.text: बद्ध्वा च अम्भोनिधिम् अशेषराक्षसकुलक्षयं कृत्वा, दशाननापहृतां भार्यां तद्वधात् अपहृताकलङ्कामपि अनलप्रवेशशुद्धाम् अशेषदेवसङ्घैः स्तूयमानशीलां जनकराजकन्याम् अयोध्याम् आनिन्ये ॥९७॥
items.tr: baddhvā ca ambhonidhim aśeṣarākṣasakulakṣayaṃ kṛtvā, daśānanāpahṛtāṃ bhāryāṃ tadvadhāt apahṛtākalaṅkāmapi analapraveśaśuddhām aśeṣadevasaṅghaiḥ stūyamānaśīlāṃ janakarājakanyām ayodhyām āninye ||97||

items.text: ततश्चाभिषेकमङ्गलं मैत्रेय वर्षशतेनापि वक्तुं न शक्यते सङ्क्षेपेण श्रूयताम् ॥९८॥
items.tr: tataścābhiṣekamaṅgalaṃ maitreya varṣaśatenāpi vaktuṃ na śakyate saṅkṣepeṇa śrūyatām ||98||

items.text: लक्ष्मणभरतशत्रुघ्नविभीषणसुग्रीवाङ्गदजाम्बवद्धनुमत्प्रभृतिभिः सम्पत्फुल्लवदनैः छत्रचामरादियुतैः सेव्यमानो दाशरथिः ब्रह्मेन्द्राग्नियमनिरृतिवरुणवायुकुबेरेशानप्रभृतिभिः सर्वामरैः वसिष्ठवामदेववाल्मीकिमार्कण्डेयविश्वामित्रभरद्वाजागस्त्यप्रभृतिभिः मुनिवरैः ऋग्यजुस्सामाथर्वभिः संस्तूयमानो नृत्यगीतवाद्याद्यखिललोकमङ्गलवाद्यैः वीणावेणुमृदङ्गभेरीपटहशङ्खकाहलगोमुखप्रभृतिभिः सुनादैः समस्तभूभृतां मध्ये सकललोकरक्षार्थं यथोचितम् अभिषिक्तो दाशरथिः कोसलेन्द्रो रघुकुलतिलको जानकीप्रियो भ्रातृत्रयप्रियः सिंहासनगत एकादशाब्दसहस्रं राज्यम् अकरोत् ॥९९॥
items.tr: lakṣmaṇabharataśatrughnavibhīṣaṇasugrīvāṅgadajāmbavaddhanumatprabhṛtibhiḥ sampatphullavadanaiḥ chatracāmarādiyutaiḥ sevyamāno dāśarathiḥ brahmendrāgniyamanirṛtivaruṇavāyukubereśānaprabhṛtibhiḥ sarvāmaraiḥ vasiṣṭhavāmadevavālmīkimārkaṇḍeyaviśvāmitrabharadvājāgastyaprabhṛtibhiḥ munivaraiḥ ṛgyajussāmātharvabhiḥ saṃstūyamāno nṛtyagītavādyādyakhilalokamaṅgalavādyaiḥ vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgabherīpaṭahaśaṅkhakāhalagomukhaprabhṛtibhiḥ sunādaiḥ samastabhūbhṛtāṃ madhye sakalalokarakṣārthaṃ yathocitam abhiṣikto dāśarathiḥ kosalendro raghukulatilako jānakīpriyo bhrātṛtrayapriyaḥ siṃhāsanagata ekādaśābdasahasraṃ rājyam akarot ||99||

items.text: भरतोपि गन्धर्वविषयसाधनाय गच्छन् संग्रामे गन्धर्वकोटीः तिस्रो जघान ॥१००॥
items.tr: bharatopi gandharvaviṣayasādhanāya gacchan saṃgrāme gandharvakoṭīḥ tisro jaghāna ||100||

items.text: शत्रुघ्नेनापि अमितबलपराक्रमो मधुपुत्रो लवणो नाम राक्षसो निहतो मथुरा च निवेशिता ॥१०१॥
items.tr: śatrughnenāpi amitabalaparākramo madhuputro lavaṇo nāma rākṣaso nihato mathurā ca niveśitā ||101||

items.text: इत्येवमाद्यतिबलपराक्रमविक्रमणैः अतिदुष्टसंहारिणो अशेषस्य जगतो निष्पादितस्थितयो रामलक्ष्मणभरतशत्रुघ्नाः पुनरपि दिवमारूढाः ॥१०२॥
items.tr: ityevamādyatibalaparākramavikramaṇaiḥ atiduṣṭasaṃhāriṇo aśeṣasya jagato niṣpāditasthitayo rāmalakṣmaṇabharataśatrughnāḥ punarapi divamārūḍhāḥ ||102||

items.text: येऽपि तेषु भगवदंशेषु अनुरागिणः कोसलनगरजानपदाः तेऽपि तन्मनसः तत्सालोक्यताम् अवापुः ॥१०३॥
items.tr: ye'pi teṣu bhagavadaṃśeṣu anurāgiṇaḥ kosalanagarajānapadāḥ te'pi tanmanasaḥ tatsālokyatām avāpuḥ ||103||

items.text: अतिदुष्टसंहारिणो रामस्य कुशलवौ द्वौ पुत्रौ, लक्ष्मणस्य अङ्गदचन्द्रकेतू, तक्षपुष्कलौ भरतस्य, सुबाहुशूरसेनौ शत्रुघ्नस्य ॥१०४॥
items.tr: atiduṣṭasaṃhāriṇo rāmasya kuśalavau dvau putrau, lakṣmaṇasya aṅgadacandraketū, takṣapuṣkalau bharatasya, subāhuśūrasenau śatrughnasya ||104||

items.text: कुशस्य अतिथिः, अतिथेरपि निषधः पुत्रोऽभूत् ॥१०५॥
items.tr: kuśasya atithiḥ, atitherapi niṣadhaḥ putro'bhūt ||105||

items.text: निषधस्यापि अनलः, तस्मादपि नभाः, नभसः पुंडरीकः, तत्तनयः क्षेमधन्वा, तस्य च देवानीकः तस्यापि अहीनकः, अहीनकस्यापि रुरुः तस्य च पारियात्रकः, पारियात्रकात् देवलो, देवलात् वच्चलः, तस्यापि उत्कः, उत्काच्च वज्रनाभः, तस्मात् शङ्खणः, तस्मात् युषिताश्वः, ततश्च विश्वसहो जज्ञे ॥१०६॥
items.tr: niṣadhasyāpi analaḥ, tasmādapi nabhāḥ, nabhasaḥ puṃḍarīkaḥ, tattanayaḥ kṣemadhanvā, tasya ca devānīkaḥ tasyāpi ahīnakaḥ, ahīnakasyāpi ruruḥ tasya ca pāriyātrakaḥ, pāriyātrakāt devalo, devalāt vaccalaḥ, tasyāpi utkaḥ, utkācca vajranābhaḥ, tasmāt śaṅkhaṇaḥ, tasmāt yuṣitāśvaḥ, tataśca viśvasaho jajñe ||106||

items.text: तस्मात् हिरण्यनाभो यो महायोगीश्वरात् जैमिनेः शिष्यात् याज्ञवल्क्यात् योगमवाप ॥१०७॥
items.tr: tasmāt hiraṇyanābho yo mahāyogīśvarāt jaimineḥ śiṣyāt yājñavalkyāt yogamavāpa ||107||

items.text: हिरण्यनाभस्य पुत्रः पुष्यः, तस्माद् ध्रुवसन्धिः, ततः सुदर्शनः, तस्मादग्निवर्णः, ततः शीघ्रगः, तस्मादपि मरुः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥१०८॥
items.tr: hiraṇyanābhasya putraḥ puṣyaḥ, tasmād dhruvasandhiḥ, tataḥ sudarśanaḥ, tasmādagnivarṇaḥ, tataḥ śīghragaḥ, tasmādapi maruḥ putro'bhavat ||108||

items.text: योऽसौ योगमास्थाय अद्यापि कलापग्रामम् आश्रित्य तिष्ठति ॥१०९॥
items.tr: yo'sau yogamāsthāya adyāpi kalāpagrāmam āśritya tiṣṭhati ||109||

items.text: आगामियुगे सूर्यवंशक्षत्रव्रतप्रवर्तयिता भविष्यति ॥११०॥
items.tr: āgāmiyuge sūryavaṃśakṣatravratapravartayitā bhaviṣyati ||110||

items.text: तस्यात्मजः प्रशुश्रुतः, तस्यापि सुसन्धिः, ततश्चापि अमर्षः, तस्य च सहस्वान्, ततश्च विश्वभवः ॥१११॥
items.tr: tasyātmajaḥ praśuśrutaḥ, tasyāpi susandhiḥ, tataścāpi amarṣaḥ, tasya ca sahasvān, tataśca viśvabhavaḥ ||111||

items.text: तस्य बृहद्बलः योऽर्जुनतनयेन अभिमन्युना भारतयुद्धे क्षयम् अनीयत ॥११२॥
items.tr: tasya bṛhadbalaḥ yo'rjunatanayena abhimanyunā bhāratayuddhe kṣayam anīyata ||112||

items.text:
एते इक्ष्वाकुभूपालाः प्राधान्येन मयेरिताः ।
एतेषां चरितं शृण्वन् सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥११३॥
items.tr:
ete ikṣvākubhūpālāḥ prādhānyena mayeritāḥ |
eteṣāṃ caritaṃ śṛṇvan sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||113||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—Sagara had two wives Sumati, the daughter of Kasyapa and Kesini, the daughter of king Viderbha. Having no offspring the king earnestly solicited the help of the sage Aurva who conferred upon him a boon that one wife should bear him a son who would keep up the race and the other sixty thousand sons; but he allowed them to make their election. Kesini chose to have one son and the other chose to have sixty thousand. Within a few days Kesini gave birth to a son named Asamanjas who upheld the family and Sumati the daughter of Vinata gave birth to a sixty thousand sons. Asamanjas had a son whose name was Ansumat.

Asamanjas was very wicked from his boyhood. His father hoped that with manhood he would reform his conduct. But he continued same even with age so his father renounced him. The sixty thousand sons of Sagara followed the example of their brother Asamanjas. The sons of Sagara having thus trodden the paths of virtue and piety in the world the celestials went to the ascetic Kapila, who was free from guilt, versed in learning and in whom was a portion of Vishnu. Having bowed unto him they said—"These sons of Sagara have followed the conduct of Samanjas. If they continue so how will the world be upheld? Thou art incarnate for the protection of the world". Hearing this Kapila said—"They shall soon be destroyed".

Thereupon Sagara undertook the celebration of a horse sacrifice. They were all engaged to look after the horse. Nevertheless some one stole the horse and carried it to the region below the earth. He then ordered them to search out the steed. Then following the impressions of its hoofs with perseverance they dug downwards each for a league. And coming to the region beneath they saw the horse walking freely. They saw at a distance Kapila, illuminating with the radiance of his person all the quarters, up and down like unto the autumnal sun freed from clouds. Then with uplifted weapons they rushed towards him, saying—"Slay him, slay him; this villain has spoiled our sacrifice; he has stolen our horse". Then turning his eyes a little Kapila looked towards them and with the sacred flame that came out of his body, the sons of Sagara were in no time reduced to ashes.

When Sagara came to know that all his sons, whom he had sent in quest of the horse, had been destroyed by the might of the sage Kapila he sent Asamanja's son to bring the animal. Ansumat, proceeding by the path which Sagara's sons had dug, arrived where Kapila was and reverentially bowing unto him so pleased him that he said—"Go my son and gave over the horse to your grand father; ask of me a boon; thy grand-son shall bring down the river of heaven on earth". Ansumat begged of the glorious Rishi a boon that his uncles, who had died on account of his displeasure although unworthy of it, might be raised to heaven. The Rishi said—"I have told you that your grandson shall bring down the Ganges upon earth. When the ashes and bones Sagara's sons shall be washed by her waters they shall be raised to heaven. Such is the glory of the stream that issues from the toe of Vishnu that they all, who bathe in it intentionally or accidentally, go to heaven. Even those shall go to heaven whose bones, skin, fibres, hair or any other part shall be left after death upon the earth which is contiguous to the Ganges". Thereupon reverentially bowing unto the sage and taking the steed, he went where his grandfather was celebrating the sacrifice. On receiving back the horse Sagara completed the sacrifice and in memory of his sons he gave the name of Sagara to the chasm which they had dug.

The son of Ansumat was Dilipa; his son was Bhagiratha who brought down the Ganges on earth, whence she is called Bhāgirathi. The son of Bhagiratha was Sruta, whose son was Nabhaga, whose son was Ambarisha, whose son was Sindhudwipa, whose son was Ayutaswa, whose son was Rituparna, the friend of Nala, well-skilled in dice; the son of Rituparna was Sarvakāma, whose son was Sudāsa whose son was Sandasa named also Mitrasaha.

Once going out on hunting, the son Sudāsa met with a couple of tigers who had cleared the forest of the deer. He killed of these tigers with an arrow. At the time of dying the form of the animal was changed and it assumed that of a dreadful and hideous fiend. And the second disappeared saying—"I shall take vengeance upon you".

After some time Saudāsa celebrated a sacrifice which was conducted by Vasishtha. At the end of the ceremony Vasishtha went out when the Raksha assuming the shape of Vasishtha said—"The sacrifice is finished to-day. You must give me flesh to eat; I shall just now come back". Having said this he went away and transforming himself into the shape of the cook prepared some human flesh. Saudāsa placing it on a dish of gold, waited for Vasishtha. As soon as the sage came back the king offered to him the dish. Thereat the sage thought—"Alas! what improper conduct on the part of the king that he is offering me flesh!" Then by virtue of his meditation he came to know that it was human flesh. Being worked up with ire accordingly he imprecated the king—"Since you have offered, though you know it, to such holy men as we are what should not be eaten, henceforth, your appetite shall be excited by similar food".

The king said—"It was yourself who commanded this food to be prepared". Vasishtha said—"By me, how could that have been". And being engaged in meditation again he found out the whole truth. Being pleased with the king he said—"The food to which I have doomed you shall not be your sustenance for ever; it shall be only so for twelve years". And the king, taking water in his palms addressed himself for cursing the sage but gave up his intention, being reminded by his queen Madayanti that it ill became him to imprecate a curse upon a holy teacher who was the guardian divinity of the family. Unwilling to throw the water upon the earth lest it should wither up the grain for it was filled with malediction and being equally unwilling to throw it up into the air lest it should blast the clouds and dry up their contents, he threw it upon his own feet. Scalded by the heat which was in the water on account of his angry imprecation the feet of the king became spotted black and white and he therefore obtained the name of Kalmashapāda (i.e. having spotted feet).

On account of Vasishtha's curse the king used to become a cannibal every third night and travelling through the forests devoured many men. Once on a time he saw a pious sage engaged in dalliance with his wife. And beholding that terrible Rākshasa form they fled away in fear but he got hold of the husband whilst they escaping. Thereupon the wife of the Brāhman begged of him her husband again and again—"Thou art the great king Mitrasaha, the pride of Ikshwaku race—not the Rākshasa. It is not proper for thee who knowest the nature of women, to carry off my husband and devour him". In vain did she lament in many ways; he devoured the Brāhman as a tiger devours a deer. Being worked up with ire the Brāhman's wife addressed the king and said—"Since, you have devoured my husband before I was satiated in his company, you shall die as soon as you shall associate with your queen". Having thus cursed him she entered the flames.

After the expiration of twelve years when he was freed of the curse, he, being desirous of dallying with his wife, thought of Madayanti who reminded him of the curse of Brahmani. He, therefore, abstained from conjugal intercourse. Being childless he solicited the help of Vasishtha and Madayanti became pregnant. The child was not born for seven years, and the queen divided the womb with a sharp stone and a son was born who was named Asmaka. The son of Asmaka was Mulaka. When the Kshatriyas were rooted out from the earth, he was concealed by a number of women, hence he was called Narikavachā (having woman for armour). The son of Mulaka was Dasaratha; his son was Ilavile; his son was Viswasaha; his son was Khatwanga, called also Dilipa, who, being invited by the gods in a war with the Asuras, destroyed a number of them. Being pleased thereby the celestials asked him to pray for a boon. Dilipa said—"If you press me to accept a boon, tell me what is the duration of my life". The god said "The length of your life is but an hour". Thereupon Khatwanga, who was gifted with great velocity, came down, in his easy-coursing car to the world of mortals. Having reached there, he prayed and said—"If my soul has never been dearer to me than the sacred Brāhmans; If I have never deviated from the satisfaction of duty; if I have never looked upon gods, men, animals, vegetables, and all created things as different from the imperishable, may I then attain unswervingly to that divine being, upon whom the holy sages meditate".

Having thus spoken he was united with that supreme being—Vāsudeva who is the preceptor of all the gods, who is abstract existence and whose form cannot be described. Thus he was united with Vāsudeva and obtained absorption.

A stanza was cited by the seven rishis in the days of yore—"There shall be no king on earth like Khatwanga. He came from heaven, dwelt an hour on earth, and became united with three worlds by means of his liberality and knowledge of truth".

The son of Khatwanga was Dirghābahu, whose son was Raghu, whose son was Aja, whose son was Dasaratha. The glorious god, from whose navel the lotus springs, was born for the protection of the world, as the four sons of Dasaratha—namely Rāma, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna. While a boy Rāma was taken by Viswamitra to protect his sacrifice and slew Tadakā. In the sacrifice, Māricha was slain and thrown away. Suvahu and others were also slain by him. He removed the iniquity of Ahalyā by merely looking upon her. Arriving at the palace of Janaka he easily broke the bow of Maheswara, and received Sitā, self-born daughter of the king Janaka as the meed for his prowess. He humbled the pride of Parusharama—the Ketu of the Haihaya race and the slayer of all Kshatriyas. At the behest of his sire and not being sorry for the loss of kingdom he went to woods accompanied by his brother Lakshmana and his wife, where he destroyed in battle Viradha, Kara, Dusana and other Rākshasas, the headless demon Kavandha and Vali the king of monkeys. Having constructed a bridge across the deep and slain all the Rākshasas, he brought back his spouse Sitā who had been carried away by the Ten-necked Rāvana. Having purified her by the fiery ordeal, and accordingly her virtue chanted by the celestials, he returned with her to Ayodhyā.
Having slain a number of Gandharvas, Bharata became the master of their country and having slain the Rākshasa chief Lavana, the son of Madhu, Satrughna took possession of their capital Muthrā.

Having thus by their unequalled might and strength the world from the grasp of the wicked, Rāma, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna went back to heaven and were followed by those inhabitants of Kosala who were one-mindedly devoted to those incarnate portions of Vishnu.

Rāma had two sons one was named Kusa and the other Lava. Lakshmana too had two sons by the name of Angada and Chandraketu. The sons of Bharata were Taksha and Pushkara. Subāhu and Surasena were the sons of Satrughna.

The son of Kusa was Atithi, whose sort was Nishadha, whose son was Nala, whose son was Nabhas, whose son was Pundarika, whose son was Kshernadhanwan, whose son was Devanika, whose son was Ahinagu, whose son was Paripatra, whose son was Dala, whose son was Chhala, whose son was Uktha, whose son was Vajranābha, whose son was Sāukanātha, whose son was Abhyuthitaswa, whose son was Viswasaha whose son was Hiranyanabha, who was a pupil of the great ascetic Jamini and imparted spiritual knowledge upon Jajnawakla. The son of this pious king was Pushya whose son was Dhruva Sandhi, whose son was Sudarsana, whose son was Agniverna, whose son was Sighra, whose son was Maru who, by virtue of his power of devotion, is still living in the village called Kalpā and who in future will be the restorer of the Kshatriya race in the solar dynasty. Maru's son was Prasusruta, whose son was Susandhi, whose son was Amarsha, whose son was Mahaswat, whose son was Visrutavat, whose son was Vrihadbala, who was slain in the great war by Abhimanyu, the son of Arjuna. These are the most illustrious kings is the race of Ikshawku. Whoever hears of account of them will be freed from all sins.
